notes: The Classic stand mixer service manual lists KSM150 without a PS suffix, so check the model plate of a KSM150PS. The manual says all solid-state Classic mixers share the same motor and control parts and have alike gears, except an 11-tooth pinion on K45SS units built before May 6, 2002.

gaps: The manual lists KSM150 without the PS suffix; it does not show that KSM150PS mixers use the same parts.
The manual covers tilt-head and bowl-lift Classic mixers and does not say which head type KSM150 is.
No thermal cut-out or overload shut-off is named in this manual, so no thermostat is claimed.
The wattmeter check (up to 135 W from STIR to speed 10 on a good mixer) is a test reading, not a rating, so no w is set; the manual gives the motor no watt or horsepower rating.
The stator coil resistances are test readings for 100-120 V, 127 V and 220-240 V units, so no voltage rating is set on the stator.
The phase control TRIAC has no part number in the manual.
No OEM part numbers appear in this manual.
Brush material is not stated (brass inserts only), so no carbon claim is made.
method: KitchenAid Classic Stand Mixer Service/Repair Manual, W11036948 (KitchenAid, 2016), 42 PDF pages, hosted as a PDF on an Amazon S3 bucket. Read as text with the research tool; page references are PDF page numbers, which match the printed numbers in the main text.
Covered-models list on page 2; the 120 VAC and universal motor statements on page 5; the control board and governor on page 6; the speed lever detents, gear case grease and bearings on page 8.
The research search found no Internet Archive copy of the service manual. A 2005 service manual (LIT4177310) is mirrored on documents.cdn.ifixit.com but was not opened.
The PartSelect KSM150PSWH0 model page returned HTTP 403 to the researcher and was not used.

comps.spec: Universal motor, AC only, 50 or 60 Hz; the manual says the Classic mixers are powered by one. Designed for 120 VAC 60 Hz (240 VAC 50 Hz on international models).
Stator with two coils. Good coils typically read about 1.5 to 2.0 ohms on 100 to 120 V units, 3.5 to 4.5 ohms on 127 V units and 8.0 to 18.0 ohms on 220 to 240 V units.
Motor brushes with springs and screw caps, running in brass inserts in the brush holders. The manual reuses brushes longer than 5/16 in and replaces shorter, unevenly worn or fouled ones.
Armature with a ventilating fan on the shaft and a ball bearing. The manual has the windings tested on a growler or at a motor repair shop, and replaces the armature if the bearing is rough.
Phase control circuit: a TRIAC on a heat sink, screwed to the bearing bracket with one 4-40 pan head screw. No part number is given.
comps.loc: On the bearing bracket, at the rear of the motor

comps.spec: Speed control board: a moveable plate carrying three contact switches (a power switch and two w-bar speed switches).
Centrifugal governor on the armature shaft: weight arms, a yoke, a ball plate and a governor spring. Its back-and-forth movement with motor speed is what the control board reads.
Speed selector lever (the switch lever), with detents at STIR, 2, 4, 6, 8 and 10.
Gear case, lubricated with 6 oz by weight of Benalene 930-2 grease.

Worm gear bracket assembly: a nylon worm gear and pinion on a bracket located by two dowels. The pinion has 10 teeth, or 11 on K45SS units built before May 6, 2002. If any part is worn the manual replaces the whole bracket assembly.
Planetary: a body with its bearing built in, an agitator shaft and a pinion gear. If the shaft has play, the manual replaces the body and shaft together.
Internal gear in the bottom cover; it can be pried out and is replaced if heavily worn or damaged.
Center bevel gear on the vertical center shaft, and the attachment hub bevel gear. The manual replaces the hub gear if its teeth are worn.
Front armature shaft bearing: a sealed ball bearing in the mixer housing. The rear motor bearing and beater shaft bearing are oil impregnated.
Power cord with a molded strain relief that slides out of a slot in the bottom cover.
